title: Kiln local qualification workload
description: Closed, source-bound contract for one deterministic local qualification workload. JSON Schema validates the wire shape; scripts/qualification/workload.py additionally enforces placeholder delivery, bounded execution, canonical ordering, result ownership, and comparison semantics.

schema_version.description: Workload contract version. The validator accepts only version 1.

workload_id.description: Stable identifier recorded in each case result and qualification receipt.

kind.description: Purpose of the workload. The kind constrains seed delivery and which comparison modes are valid.

description.description: Human explanation of the behavior, boundary, or performance claim being qualified.

determinism.description: Seed, repetition, ordering, concurrency, and network rules owned by the runner.

variables.description: Sorted declarations for operator-supplied scalar placeholders. Every declaration must be consumed, and every required variable must be consumed by every variant.

variants.description: Sorted backend/configuration variants. Each variant runs its cases serially in declared order.

comparison_policy.description: Explicit metric comparison contract, or null only for environment and soak workloads.

id.description: Lowercase stable identifier, 3–128 characters, using letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens.

nullableScalar.description: Finite JSON scalar or null. The semantic validator rejects non-finite numeric values.

configValue.description: One finite scalar, null, or recursively nested configuration object.

configObject.description: Configuration tree whose lowercase keys can be addressed as dot-separated comparison paths.

determinism.description: Runner-enforced execution envelope. Cases are serial, ordered, offline, and bounded.

seed.description: Non-negative workload seed. It is null only for environment workloads.

seed_delivery.description: How every variant receives the seed. argv and environment require the reserved ${seed} placeholder in the corresponding surface.

repetitions.description: Number of times the runner executes the declared case sequence.

case_order.description: Cases run in the order stored in each variant.

max_parallel_cases.description: The runner executes at most one case at a time to avoid undeclared contention.

network_access.description: Cases must use committed or local inputs and cannot depend on network state.

variable.description: One operator-resolved scalar placeholder declaration. Variable names are sorted and unique; runner-owned seed and model_path are reserved.

name.description: Placeholder name without ${...}. It must not collide with a runner-owned placeholder.

description.description: Operator-facing meaning and unit of the value.

type.description: Exact JSON scalar type accepted by parameter resolution.

required.description: Whether the operator must supply the value. Required variables must use a null default and be consumed by every variant.

default.description: Optional resolved value when required is false. It must satisfy the declared type and constraints.

constraints.description: Complete type-aware bounds. Unused bound kinds remain explicitly null.

allowed_values.description: Canonical sorted, unique allowed values of the declared type. An empty list means no enumeration restriction.

minimum.description: Inclusive finite lower bound for integer or number variables; null otherwise.

maximum.description: Inclusive finite upper bound for integer or number variables; null otherwise.

pattern.description: Full-match regular expression for string variables; null for numeric and boolean variables.

outputAssertion.description: Regular-expression assertion applied to a case's captured output. Duplicate assertions are rejected.

stream.description: Captured stream against which the regular expression is evaluated.

match.description: Whether the pattern must occur or must not occur.

pattern.description: Valid regular expression evaluated by the qualification runner.

case.description: One bounded argv-based command and its exact exit, output, and structured-result contract.

id.description: Stable result identifier. Compared variants must declare identical case/result contracts.

description.description: Human explanation of the operation and its expected evidence.

required.description: Whether a skip or failure makes qualification fail. At least one case per variant must be required.

command.description: Argument vector executed without shell-string evaluation. A placeholder must occupy a complete argument; the executable cannot be a placeholder.

working_directory.description: Repository-relative POSIX path. Absolute paths, backslashes, and parent traversal are rejected.

environment.description: Case-owned environment additions. Runner-owned variables cannot be overridden, and placeholders must occupy complete values.

timeout_seconds.description: Per-execution deadline in seconds. The semantic validator also caps aggregate declared wall time.

expected_exit_codes.description: Unique accepted process exit codes in ascending order.

output_assertions.description: Required and forbidden patterns checked after command completion.

result_protocol.description: Ownership and declared metric names for the strict case-result file.

producer.description: runner synthesizes only reserved process metrics; command must write its declared non-runner metrics.

path_environment_variable.description: Runner-owned variable containing the exclusive result-file path.

declared_metrics.description: Sorted, unique metrics this case owns. Runner and command metric namespaces cannot overlap.

variant.description: One backend and effective-configuration selection with a complete serial case list. Variant IDs are sorted and unique.

id.description: Stable variant identifier used by parameter resolution and comparison endpoints.

description.description: Human explanation of the backend or configuration selection.

backend.description: Portable backend family. The contract does not select a machine model.

device_requirement.description: Whether the selected backend device must exist. Accelerator variants must use required.

skip_policy.description: How an unavailable case is classified. A required device forces fail.

effective_config.description: Resolved, comparison-visible configuration tree for this variant. Non-empty trees require command-produced results.

cases.description: Non-empty serial case list. Compared variants must expose identical required flags, producers, and declared metrics by case ID.

variantPair.description: Same-backend A/B endpoint pair. Both variants must consume the same variables and declare identical result contracts.

allowed_effective_config_differences.description: Sorted dot paths that must exactly equal the scalar leaf differences between baseline and candidate effective_config.

backendPair.description: Canonical cross-backend correctness pair. Endpoints use different backend families but identical variables, effective configuration, and result contracts.

backend_a.description: Backend family for canonical endpoint A.

variant_a_id.description: Variant whose declared backend must equal backend_a.

backend_b.description: Different backend family for canonical endpoint B.

variant_b_id.description: Variant whose declared backend must equal backend_b.

allowed_environment_differences.description: Sorted environment-identity paths acknowledged as expected backend differences. This list does not relax metric equality.

metricRule.description: One required or advisory comparison over a metric declared by a required case in every selected endpoint.

scope.description: Metrics are owned by one case result.

result_id.description: Required case ID that declares the named metric in every compared variant.

metric.description: Exact metric key emitted by the declared result producer.

metric_class.description: Evidence class. Cross-backend rules allow correctness only; performance modes require performance.

unit.description: Unit attached to every metric observation. Runner-owned metrics have fixed canonical units.

aggregation.description: Declared reduction across repetitions. Runner-owned metrics have fixed canonical aggregations.

lower_is_better.description: Metric direction used to validate one-sided operators.

operator.description: Candidate comparison: equality within tolerance, no greater than baseline, or no less than baseline.

absolute_tolerance.description: Non-negative tolerance in the declared unit.

relative_tolerance.description: Non-negative fractional tolerance relative to the baseline magnitude.

required.description: Whether a failed or missing comparison makes the verdict fail. A non-empty rule set needs at least one required rule.

comparisonPolicy.description: Closed declaration of which receipts may be compared and how each result metric decides pass or fail.

mode.description: Comparison topology. Environment and soak workloads omit the policy; self-contained correctness uses command assertions without metric pairs.

variant_pairs.description: Same-backend A/B pairs, used only by declared_ab_variants.

backend_pairs.description: Cross-backend endpoint pairs, used only by cross_backend_correctness.

metric_rules.description: Metric verdict rules. Performance comparisons require command-produced performance evidence; cross-backend correctness requires equal, required correctness rules.
